# Game model (ARC-style connect-the-pieces)

## Board
- 512x512 image. Logical grid: 24px cells, origin (16,16), 20x20 cells.
  Cell (col c, row r) => pixel x=16+24c .. 16+24c+24, center (28+24c, 28+24r).
- Background = flat checkered color (changes per level).
- Pieces are solid colored polyominoes (white/green/yellow/blue...) each having
  RED 1x1 prong cells attached on their outside.

## Actions
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = move active piece up/down/left/right by exactly 1 cell (24px).
- ACTION5 = rotate active piece 90° CLOCKWISE (down->left->up->right) about its bbox center.
- ACTION6 = click coordinate; clicking empty space did nothing in level 1
  (likely selects a piece when clicked on one - untested).
- ACTION7 (undo) not offered so far. RESET not available mid-run.
- Top dark bar (x128..384, y0..10) fills WHITE from left as a budget/timer;
  it advanced on ACTION5 and on some moves. Resets each level.

## Win condition (level 1 evidence)
- Move/rotate a piece so its RED prong cells land EXACTLY ON the other piece's
  RED prong cells (they overlap/merge). Merely touching (adjacent) is not enough.
- On success: progress increments, new level loads.

## Level 1 solution recap
White arch (prongs down) vs green ring (2 prongs on its left edge, 1-cell gap
between them). Rotated white 3x CW so prongs faced right, then moved so prong
cells coincided with the green prong cells.

## Level 2 (current)
Orange bg, 4 pieces: white (top-left), green (top-right), yellow (center),
blue (bottom-right); each with red prongs. Presumably all must be joined.

# Game model: connect-the-prongs assembly puzzle (6 levels)

## Board / coordinates
- 512x512 image; logical grid = 24px cells, origin (16,16), 20x20 cells.
  cell(c,r) -> pixels x=16+24c..+24, y=16+24r..+24; center = (28+24c, 28+24r).
- Top dark bar = budget/timer that fills white over time; not fatal so far.

## Pieces
- Each piece = colored body cells + RED prong cells (1-cell protrusions).
- Exactly ONE piece is "active" at a time.
  * Levels 1-2 style: active piece rendered WHITE, others in own colors.
  * Levels 3-6 style: active piece rendered in own color, others DARK GRAY (#333333)
    with prongs hidden.
- ACTION6 click on a piece = select it (click on the active piece deselects).
  Clicking a cell where pieces overlap prioritizes the currently selected piece.

## Controls
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = move active piece up/down/left/right by 1 cell.
- ACTION5 = rotate active piece 90 deg CLOCKWISE; the bbox TOP-LEFT corner stays fixed.
  (vector rotation CW: (x,y)->(-y,x))
- ACTION6 x,y = select piece / click special cell.
- No RESET/undo available mid-run.

## Physics
- Pieces pass through each other freely (no collision). Only final config matters.
- A JOINT forms iff two prong cells of DIFFERENT pieces occupy the same cell
  (direction irrelevant). Joint cell renders gray (#666666).
- Moving a piece breaks its joints; connected pieces do NOT move together.
- WIN when EVERY prong of every piece is in a joint (all prongs paired).

## Special: WHITE cell = GROW button (level 5)
- A piece may have a WHITE cell. Clicking it while that piece is selected EXTENDS the
  piece by one segment (adds body + a new prong) and moves the white cell outward.
- Repeat until the white cell disappears = piece fully grown. Growth is needed to make
  the prong counts/geometry solvable (a "key" that must be extended to fit the locks).

## Solving method
1. Read every piece: select each, read its cells (body/prong/white) on the 24px grid.
2. Grow any white-cell piece fully first.
3. Prong bookkeeping: total prongs must be even; #joints = total/2.
   For pieces X,Y a double joint needs matching internal prong-difference vectors.
   A piece can host k prongs of another piece only if it has prongs with the same
   relative offsets.
4. Solve for rotations+translations so all prong pairs coincide; then move each piece
   once (order irrelevant; last move completes the level).
5. Minimize actions: cost = sum of L1 distances + rotations + selection clicks;
   choose the global translation (median) that minimizes the total.

# Connect-the-prongs assembly game — SOLVED (6/6 levels, WIN at turn 235)

## Board / coordinates
- 512x512 image; logical grid = 24px cells, origin (16,16), 20x20 cells.
  cell(c,r) -> pixels x=16+24c, y=16+24r; center = (28+24c, 28+24r).
- Top dark bar = a slowly filling budget/timer; never became fatal.

## Pieces & rendering
- Piece = colored body cells + RED prong cells (1-cell protrusions) [+ optional WHITE cell].
- Exactly one piece is "active".
  * L1-L2 style: active rendered WHITE, others in own colors (prongs visible).
  * L3-L6 style: active rendered in own color, others DARK GRAY with prongs hidden
    -> you must click each piece once just to read its prongs.
- Joint cell (two prongs coinciding) renders gray #666666.

## Controls
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = move active piece 1 cell up/down/left/right.
- ACTION5 = rotate active piece 90° CW about its bbox; the bbox TOP-LEFT stays fixed.
  Vector rotation CW: (x,y) -> (-y,x).
- ACTION6 x,y = click: selects the piece under the cursor (clicking the active piece
  deselects it). If pieces overlap, the ACTIVE piece has click priority.
- No RESET/undo during a run.

## Physics / win rule
- Pieces pass through each other (no collision); only the final configuration matters.
- A JOINT forms iff prong cells of two DIFFERENT pieces occupy the same cell
  (facing direction is irrelevant). Prong-over-body does NOT connect.
- Moving a piece breaks its joints; joined pieces do not move together.
- WIN when EVERY prong of every piece is in a joint.

## WHITE cell = GROW button (levels 5-6)
- Clicking the white cell of the SELECTED piece extends that piece by one segment
  (adds body cells, sometimes a new prong) and moves the white cell outward.
- Keep clicking until the white cell disappears = piece fully grown.
- Growth is mandatory: prong counts/geometry only become solvable when fully grown
  (e.g. L5: key went 3 -> 7 prongs; L6: one key 2 -> 6 prongs, one 3 -> 3 prongs).

## Efficient solving procedure
1. Click each piece once; read all cells on the 24px grid (body/prong/white).
2. Fully grow every white-cell piece FIRST (each click = 1 action).
3. Count prongs (must be even); #joints = total/2.
4. Build the connection graph: piece X can host k prongs of piece Y only if X has k
   prongs whose relative offsets equal Y's (under one of the 4 rotations).
   Multi-joint pairs need matching internal prong-difference vectors; cycles impose
   closure constraints (sum of the internal vectors around the cycle must match).
5. Solve rotations + translations, then move each piece exactly once.
   Cost = sum L1 distances + rotations + selection clicks; pick the global translation
   (coordinate-wise median) that minimizes total moves; keep one piece fixed if possible.
6. Order pieces so the last move closes the final joints.

[After action · message]
**Game complete: WIN, 6/6 levels.**

Summary of the model I built and used:

- **Core rule:** every piece is a polyomino with red *prong* cells; a joint forms only when two prongs of different pieces occupy the exact same 24px grid cell (direction irrelevant, prong-over-body doesn't count). The level ends when **all** prongs are paired.
- **Controls:** ACTION1–4 move the active piece one cell, ACTION5 rotates 90° CW keeping the bbox top-left fixed, ACTION6 selects a piece (active piece is highlighted; others render dark in later levels).
- **Physics:** pieces pass through each other, so only the final configuration matters — which let me compute each level's assembly algebraically (matching prong-offset vectors, checking cycle-closure constraints) and then move each piece exactly once along a cost-minimizing (median) global placement.
- **Late-game twist:** the WHITE cell found in levels 5–6 is a **growth button** — clicking it extends the "key" piece and adds prongs. Level 5 was provably unsolvable with the original prong set; growing the key from 3 to 7 prongs made the 7-joint solution exist. Level 6 then fell out with zero rotations once both keys were fully grown.
